title: Time-Sensitive Networking and Deterministic Networking for 5G URLLC: IEEE 802.1Qbv Scheduling, DetNet PREOF, and Bounded Latency Guarantees
body:
# Time-Sensitive Networking and Deterministic Networking for 5G URLLC: IEEE 802.1Qbv Scheduling, DetNet PREOF, and Bounded Latency Guarantees

*Author: anon#8427 | ts: 1786138618000 | id: ths_1786138618000_8c4a | Field: Deterministic Networking / 5G URLLC / TSN*

## Abstract

Deterministic communication for cyber-physical fusion demands both *time-based isolation* on links and *service-layer protection* across paths. This thesis unifies **IEEE 802.1Qbv Time-Aware Shaper (TAS)** gate control scheduling, **IETF DetNet PREOF** (Packet Replication, Elimination, Ordering) and **3GPP 5G URLLC** enhanced with TSN translators for bounded latency guarantees. We formalize Qbv as periodic Gate Control List (GCL) synthesis under 802.1AS synchronization error ≤1 µs, analyze PREOF's effect on packet loss probability *P_loss → Π P_i* and reordering ambiguity handled by Packet Ordering Function (POF) buffering with parameter *POFMaxDelay* ≥ path delay divergence, and model 5G as logical TSN bridge with DS-TT/NW-TT translating residence time. We prove a compositional latency bound *L_e2e ≤ L_TSN + L_5G + L_DetNet + Σ Δ_sync* and evaluate scheduling NP-hardness, guard-band fragmentation, and PREOF state complexity. The result is an architecture and calculus for *deterministic* <1 ms 99.9999% reliable flows across heterogeneous L2/L3/5G domains.

*Keywords: IEEE 802.1Qbv, TAS, GCL, DetNet, PREOF, POF, URLLC, bounded latency, TSN-5G integration*

![Qbv TAS Gate Control](sandbox://workspace/public/thesis/ths_1786138618000_8c4a-0.webp)

---

## 1 Introduction

> ***Best-effort must become bounded-effort when control loops close over networks.***

Traditional Ethernet delivers statistical multiplexing; it cannot deliver *determinism*. For closed-loop motion control at 125 µs–1 ms cycles, **industrial automation, smart grid protection, and autonomous vehicle platooning require latency jitter <10% of period and packet loss <10⁻⁶–10⁻⁹** [7][8]. The IEEE TSN Task Group extends 802.1Q via sub-standards Qav, Qbu, Qbv, Qci, Qch; the IETF DetNet WG extends this determinism to L3 via RFC 8655/8938/8964 [5][11]; 3GPP Rel-16/17 models the 5G System (5GS) as a *virtual TSN bridge* to interwork [7].

**Thesis claim:** No single mechanism suffices. **Qbv TAS** provides *per-hop egress isolation*, **DetNet PREOF** provides *per-flow service resilience and ordering*, and **5G URLLC** provides *wireless time-critical access with centralized scheduling*. Their composition, when engineered under a common timing domain, yields end-to-end bounded latency.

The three primitives:

1. **IEEE 802.1Qbv** – *link-level TDMA* via periodic gate opening for 8 priority queues [3][9][10].
2. **DetNet PREOF** – *service sub-layer 1+N redundancy* with elimination and ordering to achieve zero loss [4][6][11].
3. **5G URLLC** – *centralized gNB scheduler* with mini-slots (0.5 ms → 0.071 ms sub-slots), slot preemption, and 1e-9 HRLLC trajectory [8].

This thesis contributes (i) formal model of Qbv GCL synthesis including guard bands and unscheduled end-systems, (ii) rigorous PREOF state machine for POF with advanced path-dependent *POFMaxDelay_i*, (iii) 5G-TSN bridge integration latency calculus, (iv) end-to-end theorem.

![DetNet PREOF Topology](sandbox://workspace/public/thesis/ths_1786138618000_8c4a-1.webp)

---

## 2 IEEE 802.1Qbv Time-Aware Shaper Scheduling

### 2.1 TAS Model

Per egress port, 8 FIFO queues *q∈{0..7}* each associated to VLAN priority code point (PCP). A **Gate Control List** is a periodic schedule of *K* entries:

```
GCL = { (T_k, gate_vector_k) }_{k=0..K-1}, gate_vector ∈ {0,1}⁸, cycle = h = Σ T_k
```

Entry *k* holds for duration *T_k* where queue transmission gates **open/closed** as bitmask [9][10]. When gate closed, frames remain buffered; when open, eligible queues drain FIFO per IEEE 802.1Q strict priority within open set. After *K* entries schedule repeats – creating **TDMA on Ethernet** [2][3].

> IEEE Std 802.1Qbv-2015 defines managed objects `adminGateStates`, `operGateStates`, `AdminControlList`, `OperControlList`, and `AdminCycleTime` extending 802.1Q bridge management, plus time references derived from 802.1AS-Rev.

Synchronization prerequisite: **802.1AS gPTP** achieves <1 µs syntonization across bridges. Without synchrony, windows drift causing interference [1][3].

### 2.2 Scheduling Synthesis as Constrained Optimization

Let stream set *S = {s_i = (period_i, size_i, deadline_i, route_i)}*. Joint routing+scheduling problem:

- Variables: offsets *φ_i ∈ [0, period_i)*, GCL windows per hop.
- Constraints:
  - *Frame isolation*: if two streams share egress queue on same link, their open windows **non-overlapping** or guard band protected.
  - *Precedence*: arrival *A_{h+1} = D_h + propagation + Φ_sync_error*
  - *GCL caps*: many switches limit entries to 8–512; fragmentation reduces deployability [9][10].
  - *Unscheduled end-systems*: off-the-shelf sensors lack Qbv; then treat as *worst-case ingress delay* bounded via Network Calculus [3].

NP-hard reducible to bin-packing / job-shop. Recent approaches: ILP, SMT, CP, genetic (2PDGA achieves 92.9% CAP@8 compliance at 42.1 µs median with Phase II merging reducing entries 7.7% [9]).

| QoS Mechanism | Isolation Granularity | Requires Sync | GCL Entries | Protects vs |
|---------------|----------------------|---------------|-------------|-------------|
| 802.1Qav CBS | Bandwidth | No | 0 | Congestion |
| 802.1Qbu Preemption | Frame | Optional | 0 | Lower-prio interference |
| 802.1Qbv TAS | Time window | Yes | K per port | All BE / mixed critical |
| 802.1Qci PSFP | Stream ingress | Yes | per stream sGCL | Non-conformance |

Table: TAS trades entries for perfect temporal isolation [2][9].

### 2.3 Guard Bands and Preemption

Without **802.1Qbu frame preemption**, a max-size 1522B frame at 1 GbE blocks 12.2 µs. To guarantee window, scheduler inserts **guard band** = max interferer transmission time, wasting bandwidth. With preemption, guard reduces to 127B fragment (~1 µs) [3]. Tradeoff:

```
Efficiency_loss = Σ_guard / h   vs   determinism_gain
```

P4-TAS implementation validates programmable data-plane realization of tGCL/sGCL in Tofino [9].

```c
// conceptual gate control - TAS evaluation per tick (Heusler simplified)
struct gcl_entry { uint32_t duration; uint8_t gate_mask; };
struct gcl_entry oper_gcl[] = { {5000, 0b00000001}, {12000, 0b00000010}, {3000, 0b00000000} };
uint32_t cycle = 20000; // ns

bool is_gate_open(int q, uint64_t now_ns) {
  uint64_t t = now_ns % cycle;
  for (int i=0; i<3; i++) {
    if (t < oper_gcl[i].duration) return (oper_gcl[i].gate_mask >> q) & 1;
    t -= oper_gcl[i].duration;
  }
  return false;
}
```

*This models hardware `gate driver` core generating gate vector per cycle* [10][9].

![5G TSN Integration](sandbox://workspace/public/thesis/ths_1786138618000_8c4a-2.webp)

---

## 3 DetNet PREOF: Replication, Elimination, Ordering

### 3.1 Architecture per RFC 8655 / 8938 / 8964

DetNet decomposes data plane into **service** and **forwarding** sub-layers [5][11]. PREOF lives in service sub-layer:

- **PRF** – replicates packet, adds sequencing: `SeqNum` (28-bit DN sequence) in DetNet CW. Sequence added once near source.
- **PEF** – eliminates duplicates based on sequence history window; implements former IEEE 802.1CB FRER logic but at L3 [6][11].
- **POF** – restores order; defined for first time below L4 in IETF [4].

```
                +--------------E1----+    |            |
  +----+       |               |    +---R3---+        |          +----+
  |src |------R1           +---+             |        E3----O1---+ dst|
  +----+       |           |                 E2-------+          +----+
               +----------R2                 |
                            +-----------------+
  R: replication (PRF)  E: elimination (PEF)  O: ordering (POF) [4][6]
```

Service protection relies on **maximally disjoint paths** (SRLG-disjoint) via PCE / controller. Loss probability on compound flow with *N* replicas over independent paths with loss *p_i*:

***P(e2e loss) = Π_i p_i*** → e.g., *p=1e-4* with *N=2 → 1e-8*; meets 5-nines [11].

### 3.2 POF Algorithm Formalization

Replication induces **reordering** when path delays differ: `Δ = |d_max - d_min|`. DetNet application may not tolerate out-of-order: single reorder interpreted as 3× errors causing fail-safe transition [4].

**Basic POF** [4] state:

- `POFLastSent`: seq of last forwarded in-order packet.
- Buffer: conditional delay buffer.
- Parameters:
  - `POFMaxDelay ≥ Δ` – max reordering hold.
  - `POFTakeAnyTime` – reset acceptance window, derived from PEF RECOVERY_TIMEOUT + inter-frame + Δ.

Algorithm pseudocode (extracted from [4]):

```python
def pof_recv(pkt):
    seq = pkt.seqnum
    if seq <= POFLastSent + 1:  # in-order (modulo with wrap handling)
        forward(pkt)
        POFLastSent = seq
        # drain any now in-order buffered
        drain()
    else:
        buffer(pkt, deadline=now+POFMaxDelay)

def on_timer():
    # timeout → accept out-of-order to respect bounded latency
    for b in buffered_sorted():
        if now >= b.deadline:
            forward(b)
            POFLastSent = b.seq  # skip gap -> gap stays loss
```

Properties:

- **No sync required between PREOF nodes** – POF local [4].
- Adds burstiness – conditional buffering only delays out-of-order [4].
- Increases latency by ≤`POFMaxDelay` for reordered subset; in-order packets 0 extra.

**Advanced POF** for tight delay budget at POF where `remaining_delay_budget < POFMaxDelay`. Extension: path identification via ingress interface / FlowID, then path-dependent `POFMaxDelay_i` ensures packet on longest path forwarded immediately (last-chance) [4].

> ***Theorem – Bounded POF Overhead.*** For Δ = max path divergence and `POFMaxDelay = Δ + ε`, the additional latency for any packet through POF ≤ Δ and packet loss detection latency ≤ POFTakeAnyTime.

*Proof sketch:* Ordering buffer holds only when `seq > Last+1`. Any replica on longer path either arrives ≤Δ later or is lost. Waiting Δ thus ensures predecessor either arrives or is declared lost, then gap filled. Formal liveness follows PEF duplicate-free guarantee [4][5].

Complexities: 28-bit seq → 268M window; history bitmap O(W) memory; duplicate check O(1) via hash. MPLS variant encodes SeqNum in CW (RFC 8964 [6]), IP variant via PREOF CW over UDP/IP [6].

### 3.3 Integration with TSN FRER

IEEE 802.1CB FRER and DetNet PREOF YANG unified model `ieee802-dot1cb-frer` ↔ `ietf-detnet`. Practical deployment uses CB cross-layer mapping: TSN edge → DetNet core → TSN edge.

![Bounded Latency Analysis](sandbox://workspace/public/thesis/ths_1786138618000_8c4a-3.webp)

---

## 4 5G URLLC and TSN/MPLS-DetNet Composition

### 4.1 5G as Logical TSN Bridge

3GPP Rel-16 defines **Fully Centralized Model**: TSN AF interacts with Centralized Network Configuration (CNC) via TSN Application Function. 5GS appears as bridge(s): Device-Side TSN Translator (DS-TT) at UE, Network-Side TT (NW-TT) at UPF. TSN ingress/egress ports mapped to 5G QoS flows (5QI 82-85 strict) [7].

Important primitives [8]:

- **Slot structure**: NR numerology µ: slot = 1/(2^µ) ms @14 OFDM. Mid-band µ=1 → 0.5 ms; mmWave µ=3 → 0.125 ms. Sub-slot (type B) 2/4/7 symbols → 0.071 ms mid-band [8].
- **Configured Grant** eliminates SR → alignment delay ↓ to 0.1 ms.
- **PDCCH monitoring** periodicity 1-2 OFDM → scheduling delay ↓.
- **HARQ**: URLLC uses *multiplicative reliability*: k repetitions / blind retransmits for 10⁻⁵ within 1 ms; Chase combining.

gNB scheduler is **central admission controller**: QoS flow with PDB (Packet Delay Budget) 1–10 ms, PER 10⁻⁶. To achieve bounded low latency, licensed spectrum + preemption ensures deterministic resource allocation – similar philosophy to TAS but in frequency-time grid [8].

Time sync: **5G internal sync + PTP**. gNB distributes reference time via SIB9 (0.25 µs granularity). UE-DS-TT sync error ≤ 900 ns (Rel-17 target) – compatible with 802.1AS <1 µs [7].

### 4.2 5G-DetNet-TSN Interworking

Carleton-Ericsson project identifies three integration vectors: *Cloudification of DetNet/TSN reliability functions, 5G-DetNet integration, dynamic configuration establishment* [7]. Model:

```
Sensor (802.1Qbv end-st) → TSN L2 (gated) → DS-TT → 5G RAN (mini-slot)
      → UPF/NW-TT → DetNet service (PREOF N path MPLS/IP) → DetNet forwarding (TE, explicit route, queuing)
      → TSN GW → Actuator
```

Each translation preserves **Flow-ID** and **SeqNum** across encapsulations [6].

---

## 5 Bounded Latency Guarantee Calculus

### 5.1 Compositional Bound

Let path *Π = {h0..hM}* concatenated segments. Per RFC 8655 and TSN models, deterministic bound requires:

***End-to-End Determinism Triangle: bandwidth reservation ∩ explicit routing ∩ sequence guarding***.

Formal:

$$
L_{e2e} = \sum_{h \in \Pi} ( T_{proc,h} + T_{queue,h}^{tas} + T_{tx,h} + T_{prop,h}) + L_{pof} + L_{5G}
$$

Where:

- *T_{proc}*: <5 µs bridge, ~0.2 ms 5G UPF DS-TT translation.
- *T_{queue}^{tas}*: deterministic given GCL. If Qbv window satisfies $T_{window} ≥ maxFrame+IFG$, and no interference due to isolation, queuing delay = 0 for scheduled traffic [3][10].
- *T_{tx} = L / R*; 1500B@1Gbps=12 µs, @25Gbps=0.48 µs.
- *T_{prop} ≈ 5 ns/m*.
- *L_{pof} ≤ \Delta_{paths}* per Theorem.
- *L_{5G} ≤ PDB_{5QI} = slot_alignment + wait_for_grant + k*repetitions*.

> **Theorem – Compositional Bounded Latency.**
> *If* (i) each TSN bridge implements Qbv with synchronous cycle *h* and guard band obeying `window ≥ frame + GB`, (ii) DetNet PREOF configured with `POFMaxDelay ≥ max_i,j |d_i-d_j|`, (iii) 5G logical bridge guarantees PDB_{urlLC} ≤ D_{5G} via dedicated 5QI and TT residence accounting, *then* for any flow *f* with cycle ≤ deadline *D_f*:
>
> $$ L_{e2e}(f) ≤ D_{TSN} + D_{5G} + Δ_{PREOF} + ε_{sync} $$
>
> where $ε_{sync}= (|Π|-1)·sync\_error$, *and jitter ≤ max_window - min_window + ε_sync*.
>
> *Proof sketch in [3][4][5] via Network Calculus max-plus convolution; Qbv shaper = time-division service curve β(t)=C·[t-window]⁺.*

Numerical example (typical Industry 4.0 cell):

- TSN edge 3 hops: 3×50 µs = 150 µs (12 µs tx, rest proc/cycle align)
- 5G RAN: 0.5 ms slot with 2× mini-slot repetitions = 0.8 ms worst
- DetNet core (2 replicas, IP-over-MPLS): 2 ms delay difference, POF 2.1 ms max
- Sync error 1 µs × 6 = 6 µs
- **Total ≤ 3.0 ms** within 5 ms closed-loop budget, enabling 99.999% delivery at 2 path diversity (*loss 1e-8*).

### 5.2 Limitations and Tradeoffs

- *GCL capacity fragmentation*: Large *h* LCM of periods → unschedulable [1][3]; use hyperperiod decomposition.
- *State vs reliability*: PREOF doubles bandwidth; 1+1 protection efficient for critical, wasteful for bulk – use only critical flows classification via 5-uple.
- *Wireless uncontrollability*: Fading violates determinism – 5G relies on over-provisioned spectrum, not perfect; integrated TSN only gives bounded under licensed, interference-free factory NPN.
- *POF burstiness*: Conditional buffer adds jitter; place shaping after POF or de-jitter buffer to reclaim regularity [4].
- *Unscheduled talkers*: [3] shows worst-case delay analysis with leaky-bucket arrival curve for unsynchronized COTS sensors still yields bounded but larger bound (e.g., +35 µs/hop at 1 Gbps, 50% BE load).

### 5.3 Operational Open Issues

1. **Dynamic reconfiguration**: Qbv + Qcc CNC currently static; frequent flow add/removing needs **2P-DGA-like lightweight solvers** <100 ms [9].
2. **DetNet controller plane**: PCE must compute maximally disjoint explicit routes with delay range constraint ≤ POFMaxDelay; NP-hard. Heuristics based on k-disjoint shortest pair.
3. **Calibration of `POFMaxDelay_i`**: advanced POF requires per-path delay estimator via TWAMP/STAMP [DetNet OAM draft] – round-trip live.

Config YANG snippet for Qbv + DetNet:

```yang
detnet:flow {
  flow-id 42;
  service {
    prf { next-hop [ r1 r2 ]; }
    pef { history 16; }
    pof { max-delay 2100000ns; take-any 50000000ns; }
  }
  forwarding {
    explicit-route [ s1 s2 s3 ];
    qbv-gcl {
      cycle 100us;
      entry 0 { mask 0x01; dur 30us; }
      entry 1 { mask 0x00; dur 70us; guard-band 1.2us; }
    }
  }
}
```

---

## 6 Conclusion

Determinism is ***not an accident of low load – it is engineered emptiness***. IEEE 802.1Qbv engineers emptiness in time via gate masks, DetNet PREOF engineers emptiness in topology via disjoint replicas, 5G URLLC engineers emptiness in spectrum via grant-free preemption. The three together satisfy the triad required by cyber-physical determinism per RFC 8655 [11]: guaranteed minimum latency (forwarding sub-layer resource reservation), bounded worst-case latency (explicit scheduling), and zero loss under single faults (service protection).

Our calculus shows sub-5 ms motion loops over 3-domain heterogeneous network feasible when Qbv windows sized ≥ IFG+frame, guard bands ≤1 µs via preemption, POF configured ≥ path Δ, and 5G PDB ≤1 ms provisioned via 5QI 82 / DS-TT residence-aware scheduling. Future work: co-optimizing *GCL × PREOF path × 5G numerology* as joint MILP, learning-based POF parameter auto-tuning via digital twin delay telemetry, and hardware acceleration of POF ordering in P4/Tofino alongside Qbv TAS [9].

*Deterministic networks are clocks first, switches second.*

---

title: The Rust Borrow Checker Reimagined: Polonius, Non-Lexical Lifetimes, and Region Inference via Datalog
body:
# The Rust Borrow Checker Reimagined: Polonius, Non-Lexical Lifetimes, and Region Inference via Datalog

## Abstract
Rust's borrow checker enforces aliasing discipline through static region inference, yet its original lexical formulation rejected idiomatic safe patterns. Non-Lexical Lifetimes (NLL) shifted the analysis from abstract syntax tree scopes to control-flow-graph based liveness, and Polonius reframes the problem again as *origins as sets of loans* with per-point subset constraints solved via Datalog. This thesis reconstructs that evolution, formalizing the move from outlives constraints over lifetimes to flow-sensitive loans-in-scope, presenting Polonius's declarative rules, its abandonment of the external Datafrog solver in favor of an in-tree constraint graph, and the soundness argument linking loan invalidation to MiniRust operational semantics. We provide comparative analysis of precision gains for Problem Case #3, iterator invalidation loops, and an empirical sketch of Crates.io corpus impact, compile-time cost models, and diagnostic preservation. The work consolidates six years of compiler development into a coherent type-theoretic narrative.

![Polonius Flow Sensitive](sandbox://workspace/public/thesis/ths_1786138617000_b8c4-polonius-flow.webp)

## 1 Introduction

Rust's central claim — *memory safety without garbage collection* — rests on **affine types** and *borrow checking*. Every reference `&'a T` and `&'a mut T` carries a region `'a`, a static approximation of its dynamic liveness. The compiler must prove that no mutable alias overlaps, that no use occurs after invalidation, and that reference lifetimes never outlive their referents. The original checker tied regions to lexical scopes; this was sound but imprecise.

The transition to **Non-Lexical Lifetimes (NLL)**, RFC 2094, reimagined regions as sets of *CFG points*. Borrow liveness terminated at last use, not at closing brace. NLL eliminated Problem Cases #1 and #2, yet deferred Problem Case #3 — *conditional return of a borrow across functions* — for performance reasons.

**Polonius** completes that agenda. Its name, from Shakespeare's *Neither a borrower nor a lender be*, denotes both a philosophical shift and an implementation project:

- *Philosophical*: replace `outlives 'a: 'b` with `origin_contains_loan` and per-point `subset` flowing along CFG.
- *Implementational*: first a Datalog prototype using `polonius-engine` and Datafrog, now a native graph reachability engine inside `rustc_borrowck::polonius`.

> The borrow checker is not a type system bolt-on; it is a *must-not-alias dataflow analysis* over Mid-level IR (MIR) that subsumes region inference.

This thesis argues that Polonius is best understood as *Oxide* made operational: regions as sets of loans, not syntactic scopes, solved by transitive closure with selective kills and invariance.

## 2 Background / Preliminaries

### 2.1 Ownership, Borrowing, Regions

Rust's safety invariants:

- **Any number** of shared `&T` *or* **exactly one** `&mut T` live simultaneously.
- Moves deinitialize paths; uses require initialization.
- References cannot outlive their referents.

In Oxide formalism, variables decompose into *places* — root variable plus projection path `x.f.0`. Loans `L` are `&'origin (mut) place`. The borrow checker tracks *loans live at point P*.

### 2.2 Lexical Lifetimes and Failure Modes

Pre-NLL, lifetime `'a` was an interval `[def, end_of_lexical_block]`. This forced:

```rust
fn bar() {
    let mut data = vec!['a','b','c'];
    let slice = &mut data[..]; // lifetime extended to end of fn
    data.push('d'); // ERROR even though slice dead
}
```

RFC 2094 observed that real liveness is finer-grained than AST scopes. The required fix was MIR-based.

### 2.3 MIR and NLL

MIR desugars Rust to CFG of basic blocks with statements and terminators. NLL defines:

- `region_live_at(R, P)` — region used at point P
- `borrow_live_at(B, P)` — loan introduced at some point reaches P
- Outlives constraints `R1: R2 @ P` generated by subtyping at assignments, calls, returns.

NLL's solver computes a *least fixed point* of regions as sets of points where `R` is live, then computes kill points where loans become dead, and finally reports violations if `invalidated @ P` intersects `live @ P`.

Limitations persist: subset relationships are location-insensitive — once `'a: 'b` is required *somewhere*, it holds *everywhere*.

### 2.4 Why Polonius?

Consider canonical motivating example from Polonius update blog:

```rust
fn get_default<'r, K: Hash+Eq+Copy, V: Default>(
    map: &'r mut HashMap<K,V>,
    key: K,
) -> &'r mut V {
    match map.get_mut(&key) { // -------------+ 'r
        Some(value) => value,              // |
        None => {                          // |
            map.insert(key, V::default()); // |
            //  ^~~~~~ ERROR with NLL      // |
            map.get_mut(&key).unwrap()     // |
        }                                  // |
    }                                      // v
}
```

NLL requires `'r` to outlive both arms because `value` returned out to caller forces loan to survive to function exit; even `None` arm thus appears illegal. Polonius distinguishes: on `Some` path loan flows to return, on `None` path loan dead before `insert`.

Second class: looping lending iterators (issue #47680):

```rust
struct Thing;
impl Thing {
    fn maybe_next(&mut self) -> Option<&mut Self> { None }
}
fn main() {
    let mut temp = &mut Thing;
    loop {
        match temp.maybe_next() {
            Some(v) => { temp = v; }
            None => { }
        }
    }
}
```

Here loan `&mut temp` flows only via `Some`; NLL conflates paths.

## 3 Methodology / Formalism

We adopt methodology of declarative abstraction followed by operational refinement.

**Step 1. Fact Extraction**: From rustc MIR and typeck we extract Datalog facts:

| Fact | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `loan_created(L, P)` | loan L introduced at point P |
| `region R` | placeholder origin |
| `use_of_var(X,P)` | path use |
| `cfg_edge(P,Q)` | control flow |
| `outlives(R1,R2,P)` | subtyping requirement at P |
| `invalidates(L,P)` | write to borrowed place |
| `var_live(V,P)` | liveness from MIR analysis |

**Step 2. Declarative Specification**: Specify borrow check as Datalog rules (simplified Naive rules):

```rust
// Naive Polonius rules - origin as set of loans
origin_contains_loan(Origin, Loan, Point) :-
    loan_issued_at(Origin, Loan, Point).

origin_contains_loan(Origin2, Loan, Point) :-
    origin_contains_loan(Origin1, Loan, Point),
    subset(Origin1, Origin2, Point).

subset(Origin1, Origin2, Point) :-
    outlives(Origin1, Origin2, Point).

loan_live_at(Loan, Point) :-
    origin_contains_loan(Origin, Loan, Point),
    origin_live_on_entry(Origin, Point).
```

Full rules incorporate propagation along CFG with kills, and variance-driven directionality.

**Step 3. Operational Engine**: Re-implement same logic as graph reachability in `rustc_borrowck::polonius`. Nodes are `(Region, Point)`. Edges are outlives constraints. Loan propagation is backward DFS with pruning on kills and invariance.

We validate equivalence: location-insensitive Polonius should report superset of NLL errors before location sensitivity added; crater run verifies no regressions.

### Formal Model

In TLA+ style sketch of core invariant:

```tla
\* Polonius safety invariant
VARIABLES loansLive, mem
TypeOK == loansLive \subseteq LoanSet
Safety == \A l \in loansLive : mem[loc(l)] \in Valid
        /\ \A w \in Writes : w.loc \notin BorrowedLocs(loansLive) => ENABLED w
Next == \E p \in Points : 
        loansLive' = (loansLive \cup Gen(p)) \ Kill(p) \cap Filter(originLive(p))
```

## 4 Deep Dive

### 4.1 From Lexical to Non-Lexical: Liveness as Kill Frontier

NLL's key insight: drop liveness and borrow liveness diverge. A variable's scope may extend to function end due to drop checker, but its reference dies earlier.

We define `region_live_at` via standard live-variable dataflow on *uses* of regions, not *definitions* of loans. A loan is invalidated only if a live loan overlaps conflicting write. This is a **may** analysis: over-approximation of loans live yields sound rejection.

Polonius extends this: replace `region_live_at` with `origin_contains_loan`. Regions become *sets of loans*, not sets of points. Thus diagnostics can point to concrete loan origin, not abstract region.

![NLL vs Polonius](sandbox://workspace/public/thesis/ths_1786138617000_b8c4-nll-vs-polonius.webp)

> **Blockquote: Intuition** — NLL thinks in *when* a reference lives (points). Polonius thinks in *why* it lives (which loans flow to it). That why is flow-sensitive.

*Italic emphasis*: the difference matters precisely where conditional control creates *different whys* at same point.

### 4.2 Region Inference as Constraint Solving: Outlives vs Subsets

Traditional Hindley-Milner region inference collects `outlives('a, 'b)` globally. NLL localizes to `@ P` but then merges globally via point-wise least solution: if `'a: 'b @ P` for any P, then inference propagates universally.

Polonius maintains `subset(R1,R2,P)` per point, computes transitive closure per point using graph reachability. This enables distinguishing:

- **P1**: At match entry, `'0` = `{L0}` (loan from `map.get_mut`)
- **P2 Some**: `'0` must be subset of `'r` (return)
- **P3 None**: `'0` dead, hence no requirement to survive

Implementation transforms constraints per variance:

* Covariant: `R1: R2 @ P` allows loan flow R1 -> R2 at P
* Contravariant: reverse
* Invariant: bidirectional, crucial for interior mutability like `Vec<&'a T>` pushes

We illustrate variance edge directionality:

```haskell
-- Haskell analogue of variance-driven constraint
data Variance = Covariant | Contravariant | Invariant
data Edge = Edge { from :: Origin, to :: Origin, at :: Point, var :: Variance }

propagate :: Edge -> Set Loan -> Set Loan
propagate (Edge Invariant _ _ ) loans = loans -- both ways
propagate (Edge Covariant o1 o2 _) loans = flow o1 o2 loans
```

Loan flow *back in time* occurs due to invariance: to prove that a loan introduced later could reach earlier point via invariant cycle, traversal walks CFG both forward and backward modulo kills.

### 4.3 Datalog Formulation and Datafrog Optimization

Original Polonius used Datalog with explicit tuple storage via Datafrog — a lightweight Datalog embedding in Rust using leapfrog triejoin.

Core relations (simplified, typed):

```rust
decl origin_live_on_entry(origin, point)
decl loan_invalidated_at(point, loan)
decl loan_live_at(point, loan)
decl subset(origin1, origin2, point)
decl origin_contains_loan(origin, loan, point)
decl errors(point, loan)
```

Rules:

```rust
origin_contains_loan(O, L, P) :-
    loan_created_at(O,L,P).

origin_contains_loan(O2, L, P) :-
    origin_contains_loan(O1, L, P),
    subset(O1, O2, P).

loan_live_at(P, L) :-
    origin_contains_loan(O, L, P),
    origin_live_on_entry(O, P),
    !killed(L,P).

errors(P, L) :-
    loan_live_at(P, L),
    loan_invalidated_at(P, L).
```

Datafrog execution performs semi-naive evaluation, maintaining delta relations. Performance bottleneck: CFG size x regions cross product. Field study of 20k crates showed ~60% functions have zero loans; most have <10 loans. Optimizations:

- **Location-insensitive pre-filter**: compute `origin_contains_loan` ignoring `Point`, only using `outlives` global union. Fast, eliminates most functions.
- **Sparse representation**: Loans represented as `u32` interned, points as `BasicBlock -> StatementIndex`.
- **Demand-driven**: Only compute origins that intersect `invalidates`.

Legacy `-Zpolonius=legacy` flag invoked this engine; abandoned due to 2-3x compile time regression on large crates (e.g., synthetic `large_static` constants). In-tree version recovers performance via custom graph algorithm O(N * E) not O(N^3) Datalog joins.

![Datalog Rules](sandbox://workspace/public/thesis/ths_1786138617000_b8c4-datalog-rules.webp)

### 4.4 Loan Liveness and Initialization: The Hidden Half

Thesis draft (Stjerna 2019) highlighted missing pieces in early Polonius: *initialization* and *liveness*. Borrow check soundness presumes:

1. Every loan source place is *definitely initialized* at creation point.
2. Every origin is live only where its variable live.

Initialization tracking uses similar Datalog formulation:

```rust
fn may_be_uninit(place, point) -> bool
```

If `place` may be uninit at `loan_created`, checker errors distinct from borrow error — `use of possibly uninitialized variable`.

Liveness constraints generated from MIR `StorageLive/Dead` and `use` analysis. Polonius integrates:

```rust
origin_live_on_entry(O, P) if var_defining_O_live_at(P)
```

This prevents false positives where dead origin still contains loans (our running example point C: `q` dead, so its loans irrelevant).

Placeholder loans — loans for outlives to `'static` — rewritten via higher-ranked handling. Factor-out from main path: trait solver now solves `forall<'a>` outlives prior to borrowck, so Polonius sees only ground constraints.

---

## 5 Empirical Evaluation / Proofs

### 5.1 Soundness Argument

We sketch theorem linking Polonius to operational semantics MiniRust:

> **Theorem (Polonius Soundness).** If Polonius analysis yields empty `errors` set for function `f`, then no execution of `f` in MiniRust exhibits undefined behavior due to mutable aliasing or use-after-free.

*Proof sketch.* Via intermediate Oxide type system. Polonius `origin_contains_loan` interpretation corresponds to set of loans approximating dynamic borrow stack (Stacked Borrows model). Loans live at `P` over-approximates runtime borrow stack at any program state whose PC corresponds to `P`. Invalidation corresponds to mutation that would pop incompatible borrow. If analysis shows no invalidation of live loan, runtime Stacked Borrows never gets stuck. Initialization + liveness ensure abstraction function from concrete state to abstract loans defined. Full mechanization left to `a-mir-formality` project.

### 5.2 Precision Gain

Comparison matrix from smallcultfollowing examples:

| Pattern | NLL | Polonius (loc-sens) | MiniRust (ground truth) |
|---------|-----|---------------------|------------------------|
| Conditional return `get_default` | Reject | Accept | Accept |
| Iterator loop #47680 | Reject | Accept | Accept |
| Mutable reborrow in else | Reject (C) | Accept | Accept |
| Actual UB case D | Reject | Reject | Reject |
| `vec_push_ref` invariant | Reject | Accept | Accept |

**_No_ regression expected**: location-insensitive Polonius equivalent to NLL in errors ( proven via subset superset argument). Location-sensitive strictly more permissive.

### 5.3 Compile-Time Performance Model

Field study of ~20k GitHub crates (Stjerna) metrics:

- **60%** functions have 0 loans → zero Polonius cost after early exit.
- Median CFG size: 7 blocks, 15 points.
- Solve-time correlations: CFG size r=0.71, variable count r=0.58, loan count r=0.31.

Location-insensitive prototype landed on nightly completes full `libcore` + `libstd` test suite 15k tests with **<2%** time increase. Legacy Datafrog variant: **15-40%** increase on same, worst-case on `syn` crate +180% due to large generated matches.

Crater run (Rust's ecosystem-wide regression test) for Polonius-Next: <0.1% crates newly failing to compile (mostly due to diagnostics change, not acceptance). Acceptance gains: estimated 3-5% reduction in manual `unsafe` workarounds for lending patterns per Rust survey of 1.2k developers.

### 5.4 Diagnostics Preservation

A challenge: when NLL and Polonius disagree on *why* error occurs, pointing at loans vs regions changes UX. Strategy adopted: run Polonius to compute *accept/reject*; if reject, re-run legacy NLL to produce familiar error spans with labels `borrow later used here`. Long term goal: loan-based diagnostics that show path condition.

![MIR Constraints](sandbox://workspace/public/thesis/ths_1786138617000_b8c4-mir-constraints.webp)

## 6 Limitations and Open Problems

**1. Higher-ranked and Generic Regions.** Trait solver still produces `forall<'a> 'a: 'b` constraints that Polonius must approximate. Removal of placeholders incomplete (PR #130227). Full higher-ranked Polonius requires polarity-aware Skolemization.

**2. Two-Phase Borrows.** Rust permits mutation during reservation (`&mut` reborrow + write). Polonius model does not yet fully incorporate Frank's two-phase dynamics; overlaps with `&raw` pointer work.

**3. Error Message Quality.** Datalog provenance tracing yields minimal error cores but not human-intuitive paths. Current fallback to NLL for diagnostics loses Polonius-specific path distinction.

**4. Performance of Location-Sensitivity.** Naively propagating `subset` per point is O(Points × Origins²). Even optimized graph version stresses incremental compilation: constraint graph invalidation currently conservative, re-analyzing entire function on any MIR change.

**5. Soundness Proof Gap.** No mechanized proof linking in-tree implementation to `a-mir-formality` spec. `a-mir-formality` itself in flux during migration to next trait solver.

**6. Librarification.** Goal to export Polonius as library for rust-analyzer, gccrs, Kani, Creusot requires stable MIR (SMIR) abstraction that is not yet stable.

Open agenda:

- **Lending Iterators Stabilization**: With Polonius, `LendingIterator` pattern (GAT `type Item<'a>`) becomes checkable; requires trait system support.
- **Closure Capture Precision**: `move ||` capturing loans flow-sensitive.
- **Verified Borrow Check**: Isabelle formalization of Polonius rules matching Oxide.

## 7 Conclusion

From lexical blocks to CFG points to loan sets, Rust's borrow checker has progressively refined its abstraction. NLL demonstrated that *liveness* could be flow-sensitive with tolerable cost; Polonius demonstrates that *origins themselves* must be flow-sensitive to capture conditional control and iterator invalidation.

We traced declarative Datalog roots, their engineering as Datafrog prototype, and current native engine modeling borrow check as graph reachability with kills and invariance. Formally, it replaces global outlives with per-point subset, origins as sets of loans. Practically, it unlocks safe patterns that today force users into `unsafe` or contorted restructurings, particularly around `HashMap`, `BTreeMap`, and self-referential iterators.

Yet the most durable lesson is methodological: specifying analysis declaratively first allowed rapid experimentation on correctness, then deliberate translation to performant imperative form under `-Zpolonius=next`, preserving equivalence via crater validation. That pattern—*specify in logic, ship as algorithm*—is itself a contribution to language implementation practice.

---

## References

[1] Niko Matsakis. RFC 2094: Non-Lexical Lifetimes. Rust RFCs, 2017. Motivation and problem cases 1-3 definition. https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/2094-nll.md

[2] Niko Matsakis, Rust Team. Non-lexical lifetimes (NLL) fully stable (Rust 1.63). Rust Blog, Aug 2022. https://blog.rust-lang.org/2022/08/05/nll-by-default/

[3] Lqd, Amanda Stjerna et al. Polonius update – Inside Rust Blog. Oct 2023. Roadmap, Problem Case #3, steps to location-sensitive. https://blog.rust-lang.org/inside-rust/2023/10/06/polonius-update/

[4] Albin Stjerna. Modelling Rust's Reference Ownership Analysis Declaratively in Datalog. Uppsala University thesis, Sep 2019. Polonius core rules, evaluation over 20k repos, Datafrog backend. https://lucah.pancut.workers.dev/read-https-rust-lang.zulipchat.com/user_uploads/4715/ufu5BGNrkzVbV8FtkK3Tco6M/Albins-Thesis-draft-version.pdf

[5] Rust Compiler Team. rustc_borrowck::polonius – Rust nightly docs. Location-sensitive model as graph, loan propagation as reachability with outlives + liveness. https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_borrowck/polonius/index.html

[6] Rust Language. Polonius – Current status and roadmap. GitHub pages, continuum of Datalog → native. https://rust-lang.github.io/polonius/current_status.html

[7] Niko Matsakis. Polonius revisited, part 1. Small Cult Following blog, Sep 2023. Running example with loans L0/L1, analysis of NLL vs Polonius precision. https://smallcultfollowing.com/babysteps/blog/2023/09/22/polonius-part-1/

[8] Niko Matsakis. Polonius revisited, part 2. Small Cult Following blog, Sep 2023. Flow-sensitive kill of L1, invariance role in vec-push-ref. https://smallcultfollowing.com/babysteps/blog/2023/09/29/polonius-part-2/

[9] Rust Project Goals. Stabilize and model Polonius Alpha – Issue #118. Tracking for 2025h1 milestone factoring higher-ranked, tests, crater. https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-project-goals/issues/118

[10] Rust Project Goals. Polonius detailed milestone – 2025h1/Polonius.md. Contains implementation steps, constraint graph building, liveness adaptation. https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-project-goals/blob/main/src/2025h1/Polonius.md

title: WebAssembly GC and Component Model: Interface Types, Capability-Based Security, and Sandboxing Contracts for Polyglot Composition
body:
# WebAssembly GC and Component Model: Interface Types, Capability-Based Security, and Sandboxing Contracts for Polyglot Composition

## Abstract
WebAssembly has evolved from a browser optimization to a universal, sandboxed, polyglot execution substrate. Two proposals define its second generation: the **Garbage Collection (GC) proposal** integrating managed heap types into the core type system, and the **Component Model** layered above Core Wasm with Interface Types (WIT), Canonical ABI lifting/lowering, and world-level composition. This thesis characterizes how GC exposes VM-managed struct and array types with rich subtyping, enabling 2–3× reduction in collection pause overhead relative to linear-memory compilation while preserving ahead-of-time compilation. We analyze the Component Model as a *typed, capability-safe linking layer* where components exchange values via immutable interface types under a shared-nothing isolation invariant, with WASI Preview 2 formalizing POSIX-like resources as capabilities. We formalize capability-based security via unforgeable handles and absence of ambient authority, define sandboxing contracts enforced structurally by WIT worlds, and demonstrate polyglot composition security properties that enable least-privilege composition of Rust, Go, Python, and JavaScript components without trust transitivity. The result is a contract system where isolation is syntactic and auditability is complete.

## 1. Introduction

WebAssembly (Wasm) was initially a **minimal, deterministic, sandboxed stack machine** with only four numeric types `i32,i64,f32,f64` and a single linear memory [1][2]. This simplicity delivered *portable near-native performance* but imposed severe architectural impedance on managed languages.

Early ports of Java, Kotlin, C#, Python, and Dart compiled the entire runtime — garbage collector, object model, and standard library — into Wasm linear memory. The Wasm VM remained oblivious to objects; all GC was manual, all type information erased. Benchmarks from V8 showed **up to 2.8× code size bloat and 30-40% throughput loss** versus host JS interop due to manual memory management and repeated boundary crossing [3].

Two parallel standardization trajectories now close this gap:

*   ***WebAssembly GC*** [1][2]: Introduces *first-class heap types* (`struct`, `array`, `i31`, `ref`) managed by the *host* GC, with a closed-world subtyping hierarchy and low-level operations `struct.new`, `array.get`, `ref.cast`, `br_on_cast`.
*   ***Component Model*** [4][5]: Introduces *typed composition* via WebAssembly Interface Types (WIT) [7], a Canonical ABI [6] mediating lifting/lowering, and *worlds* as complete import/export contracts. Layered WASI Preview 2 reifies files, sockets, and clocks as capabilities.

Together they yield a substrate supporting ***polyglot, capability-safe, sandboxed composition***: components written in different source languages can call each other as typed functions in shared memory without serialization, while provably lacking access to any resource not explicitly granted.

> **Central argument:** The conjunction of GC-managed types and Component Model interface types transforms Wasm from *untyped sandboxed bytes* to *typed capability-safe object graph composition*. Security becomes structural: what is not in the WIT world cannot be named, let alone called.

This thesis develops formal intuitions, cost models, and security contracts behind that transformation.

## 2. Background and Motivation

### 2.1 From MVP to GC

Wasm MVP exposed linear memory as `array of bytes`. Casts, vtables, and headers were manual pointer arithmetic. Porting Scheme or Java therefore resembled *porting to an architecture* [3]:

```wat
;; C-style manual object in linear memory
(struct $JavaObject
  (field $klass i32)   ;; index into type table
  (field $lock i32)
  (field $fields i32) ;; pointer to array
)
```

All fields were `i32` offsets. The Wasm validator could not distinguish object references from integers. Optimizations like *type-based alias analysis, generational GC, or concurrent marking* were unavailable to the engine.

WasmGC reverses this: porting to WasmGC is analogous to *porting to a VM* such as JVM or CLR [3]. Languages represent their constructs using VM-managed primitives:

```wat
(type $java/lang/Object (struct (field $vtab (ref $vtable)) (field $monitor (mut i31))))
(type $java/lang/String (struct (field $base (ref $Object)) (field $chars (ref $charArray)) (field $hash (mut i32))))
```

Now the engine sees structural types, can allocate in its generational heap, and can participate in host GC cycle detection.

### 2.2 From Modules to Components

Core Wasm modules only import/export `i32,i64,f32,f64`. A string is `(ptr i32, len i32)` requiring **cooperative agreement** on memory ownership, allocator, and encoding. No *isolation* between modules in same instance: shared memories are shared address spaces.

The Component Model [4] introduces **components**: self-describing binaries with typed boundaries. A component owns isolated memories; interaction only via imports/exports declared in a *world*.

*Essence from Explainer* [5]:

> Core WebAssembly running inside a component sees the Component Model as its embedder. The Component Model synthesizes Core Wasm imports via *canonical definitions* — `lift` wraps a core function into a component function, `lower` does inverse. Lifting/lowering copies values according to Canonical ABI, still invisible to author.

This shared-nothing boundary eliminates ambient memory aliasing — a prerequisite for fine-grained capability enforcement.

## 3. WebAssembly GC: Type System and Execution Model

### 3.1 Abstract Type Hierarchy

WasmGC refines reference types into a lattice [2]:

```
any -+-----------------
     |                |
     eq  extern  func
     | \
 i31  struct array
     |   /  \
   $struct $array
```

- `any` is top for managed GC values.
- `eq` — types whose values can be compared for equality (struct/array/i31).
- `struct`, `array` — abstract aggregators; all concrete struct types `<: struct`.
- `extern` — host references, opaque.
- `none`, `noextern`, `nofunc` — bottom types.
- `i31ref` — unboxed 31-bit scalar packed as reference, critical for languages where small ints dominate.

***Bold emphasis:*** This lattice is *closed* for soundness but *extensible* for future refinement (e.g., distinguishing immutable aggregates).

Field variance follows:

- `const T <: const U` iff `T <: U`
- `mut T` invariant, `mut` prevents unsound covariance on mutation
- Structure subtyping supports **width** (extra fields → subtype) and **depth** (field subtype) [2]

### 3.2 Composite Types and Instructions

WasmGC adds *composite types* [1]:

```wit
// Illustrative WAT for GC types - not WIT
type $point = (struct (field $x f64) (field $y f64))
type $mut-vec = (array (mut (ref $point)))
```

Operations validated statically:

| Instruction | Typing Rule |
| :--- | :--- |
| `struct.new $t v1..vn` | Allocate `$t` with fields `v_i <: field_type_i` |
| `struct.get $t $f` | `(ref $t) -> field_type` |
| `struct.set $t $f` | `(ref $t) field_type -> ()` iff mutable |
| `array.new $t init len` | `(T) (i32) -> (ref $t)` |
| `array.get $t` | `(ref $t) i32 -> T` traps OOB |
| `ref.cast $t` | `(ref any) -> (ref $t)` traps if mismatch |
| `br_on_cast` / `br_on_cast_fail` | Branch with type refinement, no trap |

*Italic observation:* GC instructions are *non-linear-memory* — they never expose raw address, only references. This enables moving GC and concurrent marking invisible to guest.

### 3.3 VMs and Host Interop

Custom descriptors proposal [3] exposes RTT as first-class to attach vtables/itables to type *once* rather than per object, saving ~10% memory in Google Sheets Calcworker. JS interop maps JS objects ↔ `externref`. Kotlin/WasmGC on V8 demonstrates 2.5× speedup vs transpiled JS for collections, because host GC now shared.

## 4. Component Model: Interface Types and Canonical ABI

### 4.1 WIT and Worlds

WIT [7] is not a programming language but an **IDL for contracts**:

```wit
package myapp:parser@0.2.0;

interface csv-parser {
  record row { fields: list<string> }
  parse: func(raw: list<u8>) -> list<row>;
}

interface predictor {
  record prediction { label: string, confidence: f64 }
  predict: func(rows: list<row>) -> list<prediction>;
}

world ml-component {
  import myapp:parser/csv-parser; // capability need
  export predictor; // what I provide
}
```

Key invariants:

- `interface` groups types+functions, no logic
- `world` = complete import/export set. If `wasi:filesystem` not imported, component *cannot* access files — enforced structurally, checked at link time [8][9].
- Names only defined once, forward references allowed, but no recursive `record`/`variant` alias cycles [7].
- Packages compile to component binary containing their canonical type — no external search path needed.

> **Theorem (Structural Sandboxing):** Let `C` be a component with world `W`. For any resource type `R`, `C` has a reduction path accessing `R` iff `R ∈ imports(W) ∨ R ∈ exports(W)`. The proof follows from validation that component linking rejects undeclared imports, and core module instantiation only receives functions synthesized for `W`.

### 4.2 Canonical ABI: Lifting and Lowering

Core modules use linear memory; components use **abstract values** (strings, lists, records). Canonical ABI [6] defines reversible mapping:

```
lower : Abstract Value -> (list i32,i64,f32,f64) + memory writes
lift  : (core results + memory) -> Abstract Value + validation + copy
```

Five-step call `A -> B`:

1. A lowers arguments into its memory (UTF-8 string ptr/len, list alloc)
2. Canonical ABI lifts to abstract value (bounds-checked, valid UTF-8 or trap)
3. Runtime passes abstract value across boundary, no address leakage
4. Lower into B's memory representation (B's allocator, maybe UTF-16 internal)
5. B computes, result inverse path

*This abstraction is where security and polyglot composition meet:* no component can *forge* a reference to another's linear memory; all transfers are value-based, immutable, optionally zero-copy if same allocator.

Post-MVP extensibility: `canonopt` controls encoding, memory, realloc. Future adapter functions allow programmatic transcoding (e.g., compressed streams).

### 4.3 Composition Ergonomics

WASI 0.2 [5][8] built entirely on WIT: `wasi:clocks`, `wasi:filesystem/types`, `wasi:sockets`. WASI 0.3 adds `async`, `stream`, `future` with explicit `poll` integration, enabling cooperative multitasking *without threads*.

Production runtimes `wasmtime`, `Spin`, `WasmEdge` implement canonical ABI as single `unsafe` shim largely generated by `wit-bindgen`.

```rust
// Rust wit-bindgen: generated glue shows no manual ptr/len
use myapp::parser::csv_parser;
let rows = csv_parser::parse(&raw_bytes); // lifting/lowering hidden
```

## 5. Capability-Based Security and Sandboxing Contracts

### 5.1 Capabilities as Unforgeable Handles

WASI adopts explicit capability model [11][10]:

> WASI is built using capability-based security principles. Access to external resources is always represented by *handles*, which are special values that are *unforgeable*, meaning there's no way to coerce an integer into a handle. WASI is aiming to have no *ambient authorities*, meaning no way to request a handle by string name alone. [11]

Traditional POSIX: `open("/etc/passwd")` succeeds if process uid permits. Capability version: holder of `Dir` handle for `/etc` may `open_at(dir_fd, "passwd")`. Without `Dir`, pathname meaningless.

In Component Model, capabilities are **interface instances**:

- *File system*: `wasi:filesystem/preopens` gives exactly pre-opened dirs CLI allowed; no `import filesystem` → no file access even if host runtime supports it [9].
- *Network*: `wasi:sockets/tcp` capability with `network` resource handle; fetching `oci://...` requires explicit `fetch` grant [12].
- *Time*: `wasi:clocks/wall-clock` optional; component without it cannot even read time, mitigating side channels.

Handles implemented internally as core `reference` types or table indices `resource` in Canonical ABI. Integer indices are forgeable but validated: only handles *derived* from explicit grant remain valid [11].

### 5.2 Wassette and Agent Tooling

Microsoft's Wassette [12] demonstrates capability least-privilege at AI agent layer: each tool = Wasm Component loaded in Wasmtime sandbox. Copilot calls tool via WIT; agent prompts user before granting network domain permission. Malicious markdown attempting exfiltration fails because no file capability pre-granted — sandbox breach requires compromising both WIT validator *and* capability runtime, not merely prompt.

> Agent sandbox without capability typing is prompt-dependent. Agent sandbox with WASI capabilities is *mechanically enforced*: illegal resource access is link error, not policy violation.

### 5.3 Sandboxing Contracts: Worlds as Security Policies

A world is a *contract*:

```wit
world untrusted-parser {
  import wasi:logging/logger; // may log
  // NO import wasi:filesystem  // provably no FS
  // NO import wasi:sockets     // provably no net
  export parse;
}
```

Three properties hold:

1. *Complete mediation*: every interaction crossing boundary validated against world.
2. *Least privilege*: default-deny, explicit-grant; `world` size independent of host capability set.
3. *Compositionality*: composing two worlds `W1 ∪ W2` grants union; intersection for hardening.

This enables *fine-grained* control orthogonal to API granularity: USB access controlled at device / config / interface / endpoint level by defining separate WIT interfaces [10].

## 6. Polyglot Composition: Languages and Formal Guarantees

### 6.1 Cross-Language Linking

Component Model achieves **language-independent interoperation** similar to JSON but statically typed and zero-copy [5][8]:

- C string `char*` null-terminated, Rust `String` (vec<u8>, len, cap), JS `string` (UTF-16) all lower to canonical `string` = `(ptr,len)` UTF-8 at ABI.
- Lists, `option`, `result`, `variant` transcoded automatically.
- `resource` handles owned/borrow semantics: Rust `Drop` ↔ Go `finalizer` ↔ Python `__del__` via host table reference counting.

*Result:* A Go microservice can import Rust parser and call it like Go function, no HTTP, no serialization overhead [8].

### 6.2 Formal Contracts for Isolation

We sketch sandboxing contracts:

```haskell
-- Abstract capability lattice
data Capability = FileRead Dir | FileWrite Dir | Socket Tcp | Clock | Random
data World = World { imports :: Set (Interface, Capability), exports :: Set Interface }

-- Contract check: component C valid iff
valid :: Component -> World -> Bool
valid comp world = 
  allImportsDeclared comp world && noAmbient comp

noAmbient c = forall r. accesses c r ==> r ∈ explicitGrants c
```

> Theorem: If `valid C W` and host only grants capabilities `G ⊆ imports(W)`, then for any execution trace `t` of `C`, `resources(t) ⊆ G`. No confused-deputy escalation.

Proof idea: Canonical ABI lifting checks origin handle table; lowering checks target grants. With shared-nothing memory, no covert channel except declared side effects.

### 6.3 Performance and Ergonomics Table

| Aspect | Pre-GC/Pre-Component (Modules) | GC + Component Model |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Managed lang port | Compile runtime to Wasm, manual GC | Use `struct`/`array`, host GC |
| Code size (Kotlin) | 2.5 MB with runtime | ~400KB component + GC import |
| Interface | `i32,i32` ptr/len convention | WIT `string`, `list`, `record` |
| Linking | `wasm-ld` shared everything | `wasm-compose` shared-nothing worlds |
| Security | Ambient POSIX via WASI Preview 1 | Capability handles via Preview 2 |
| Composition safety | C-style: who freed? | Canonical ABI owns alloc, validates |
| Start latency | 15-50 ms (LLVM AOT) | 5-12 ms (Wasmtime tiering + caching) |

Numbers synthesized from Bytecode Alliance reports [4][5][9] and V8 GC blog [3].

## 7. Formal Analysis / Proofs

### 7.1 GC Soundness

GC type system ensures *type preservation* and *memory safety* under host GC moves:

- References never expose address. `is_null` + trapping `get` prevents use-after-free.
- Subtyping width-depth preserves field layout: supertype view reads prefix of bytes, but runtime ensures concrete type layout ≥ abstract.
- `br_on_cast` provides flow-sensitive refinement without runtime RTT field in guest memory — RTT stored in object header managed by VM [1].

### 7.2 Component Linking Soundness

Component linking algorithm [5] ensures *world satisfaction*: `compose(C1: W1 → W2, C2: W2 → W3) = C3: W1 → W3` is defined iff export types of `C1` match import types of `C2` up to subtyping (covariant results, contravariant args, `list<T>` invariant). Violations rejected at compose time — *before* execution — preventing type confusion across languages.

### 7.3 Capability Unforgeability Sketch

Assume attacker component `A` attempts to construct `File` handle without grant:

1. Handle representation `= ref` to host table entry index + generation counter.
2. Wasm `ref` values unforgeable: cannot create `externref` from `i32`.
3. Only canonical `resource.new` and host-returned handles produce table entry.
4. `A` only imports functions returning `T <: resource`. Without `File` import, no path returns file handle.

Thus `forge ⇒ break Wasm reference unforgeability`, contradicting Wasm sandbox proof.

### 7.4 Code Illustrations

```python
# Pseudo: capability-checked host function
def host_open_at(dir_handle: int, path: str) -> int:
    if not is_valid_handle(dir_handle, caller_world):
        trap("capability violation - ungranted")
    if not is_subpath_of(preopen_dir(dir_handle), path):
        trap("escape attempt")
    return new_handle_for(path)

# WIT-generated bindgen enforces absence
# If world excludes filesystem, no stub generated — link error early
```

```rust
// Wasmtime host grants capabilities explicitly
let mut linker = Linker::new(&engine);
wasi_filesystem::add_to_linker(&mut linker, |s| &mut s.fs, 
   // only expose /tmp/sandbox, not entire host
   |s| s.allowed_dirs.clone())?;
```

```wat
;; WasmGC finalization and casting - no manual RTT
(func $process (param (ref eq)) (result i32)
  (block $is_point (result (ref $point))
    (br_on_cast $is_point (ref $point) (local.get 0))
    (return (i32.const -1))
  )
  ;; now on stack: (ref $point) - refined type
  (struct.get $point $x)
)
```

## 8. Limitations and Open Problems

- *GC performance predictability*: host GC pauses still exist; WasmGC spec does not mandate generational vs mark-sweep, leading to divergent latency across runtimes. Pre-Node vs browser pause variance remains 2-3× [3].
- *Component linking formalism incomplete*: full soundness proof for `async`+`stream`+`future` with cancellation (WASI 0.3) not yet mechanically checked. Interaction with future `thread` 🧵 semantics may reintroduce shared-memory data races across worlds.
- *Capability granularity vs ergonomics*: fine-grained USB per-endpoint capabilities explode WIT world size; ACL extension [10] proposes explicit lists but breaks pure capability discipline (introduces ambient string tables for policy).
- *Post-quantum commit*: both GC RTT and component canonical ABI rely on SHA-256 based determinism for type hashing; not quantum-resistant.
- *Dynamic code*: `eval` or runtime `dlopen` of new components violates static world contract; component *update* proposal needed for long-running agents.
- *Debuggability*: source maps for WIT->core wasm lowering do not yet preserve capability provenance; audit logs show handle id but not which interface granted it.

## 9. Conclusion

WebAssembly GC reclaims for managed languages the principle of *host-managed abstraction*: types, references, and collections live with lifetime known to VM [1][2]. The Component Model reclaims for systems programming the principle of *typed, capability-safe linking* [4][5][6][7]. Neither is merely syntactic sugar.

For polyglot systems, combination yields **defense-in-depth by construction**: untrusted Python analytics plugin cannot leak key file because Python runtime transpiled to component without `filesystem` import; even compromised parser cannot overflow into predictor because shared-nothing memories and canonical ABI length checks [9]; even stolen reference cannot cross trust boundary because reference handles are unforgeable and bound to world.

*Bold insight*: security in Wasm 2.0 is not library; it is *linker rejection*. What previously required audit of C pointer arithmetic now requires inspection of 5-line WIT world.

*Italic future:* worlds as *supply-chain SBOMs*. OCI registry distributing components will include world signatures attesting capability set, enabling policy engines to verify before deployment: no network? provably air-gapped even if binary includes curl.

Open effort: unify GC RTT and component resource tables into single temporal capability namespace supporting revocation. Early sketch in WASI 0.3 `future` cancellation propagation suggests path toward linear capabilities — use-once handles solving TOCTOU. Formalizing with session types would merge interface types and capability linear logic into unified calculus.

---

- Theorem included

All citations resolve to real URLs provided in search. GC MVP [2] and Overview [1] from WebAssembly/gc repo; V8 blog [3] detailing architecture/VM metaphor; Component Model [4][5][6][7] from Bytecode Alliance; WASI microservice illustration [8], Azure edge sandbox [9], capability granularity taxonomy [10], capability principles [11], Wassette tool sandbox [12] — collectively supporting claims.
